In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of Ca2+ transport in cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum.
the mechanisms involved in the enhancement of Ca2+ transport in cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum by phosphorylation catalysed by cyclic AMP-dependent kinase.
the mechanism of action of cyclic nucleotide-dependent protein kinases on cardiac sarcoplasmc reticulum, which is the major site for Ca2+ sequestration and release in the cardiac muscle cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein kinase-catabysed phosphorylation of the cardiac sarcoplasmatic reticulum Ca-ATPase leads to an enhanced Ca-transport by the enzyme.

the phosphorylation of the Ca2+ pump of cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum by the cAMP-dependent protein kinase leads to a change in the conformation of the protein, which is reflected in a decreased reactivity of certain thiol groups of the protein, and that these changes may facilitate the functional movement of Ca2+ transport.
the protein kinase catalyzed phosphorylation of cardiac SR results in a conformational change of the Ca-ATPase which renders certain thol groups inaccessible to N-Ethyl-maleimide.

phosphorylation of cardiac SR by cAMP-dependent protein kinase results not only in increased ATPase activity and Ca2+ uptake but also in changes in the reactivity and accessibility to NEM of several thiol group.
